title: Weak-adjoint rewrite of the simultaneous f-divergence derivative
source_anchor: Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling (2026-08-09), Theorem 8.3.1 proof, printed p. 219 / PDF p. 230: after differentiating the simultaneous f-divergence, use ∂t mu_t = L_t^* mu_t and ∂t nu_t = L_t^* nu_t to move each density time derivative onto the generator acting on the corresponding frozen observable.
target_statement: In the fixed dominating-measure density presentation already used by SimultaneousFDivergenceIntegral, assume the two selected-time weak adjoint pairing identities for u=f'∘rho and v=f∘rho-rho*(f'∘rho). Rewrite the integral of derivativeIntegrand as the sum of the two generator pairings. Also expose the linear-map rewrite L(v)=L(f∘rho)-L(rho*(f'∘rho)). Do not construct L*, prove a Fokker--Planck PDE, or claim the full Theorem 8.3.1.

shared_floor_audit.notes: The source's measure equation is more general than a fixed semigroup and more abstract than a common-reference density path. This cell deliberately does not redefine the adjoint generator. It accepts exactly the two weak pairing identities needed at the selected time and joins them to the already-formalized density derivative. A later bridge may derive these identities from a time-dependent weak-adjoint evolution contract; the existing WeakForwardEquation is evidence for the semantic pattern but is not silently treated as proving the general L_t case.
